newsitem.title: USA: USAA acquires $400 mln of catastrophe reinsurance.
newsitem.headline: USAA acquires $400 mln of catastrophe reinsurance.

text.p: USAA Group, one of the country's largest property insurers, said on Wednesday it acquired $400 million in catastrophe reinsurance coverage in a transaction involving the private placement of bonds.
This coverage is 80 percent of USAA's $500 million layer of reinsurance for losses in excess of $1 billion, USAA said.
In a financial transaction completed June 16, USAA was the ceding insurer to, or customer of, Residential Reinsurance Ltd, a special purpose reinsurance company, USAA said.
The reinsurer issued $477 million in one-year bonds to provide USAA reinsurance for hurricane losses in excess of $1 billion in 20 states and the District of Columbia, USAA said.
The bond offering, which was about two times oversubscribed, was sold in two tranches, which link investors' returns to the company's windstorm losses.
In one tranche, the principal was protected and in the other it was entirely at risk, the sources said.
Investors' returns on the bonds would be reduced if the company's losses from an East Coast hurricane topped $1 billion, they said.

"This transaction represents increased financial capacity for USAA in the event a severely destructive hurricane affects USAA policyholders, especially in Florida," said USAA chief executive Robert T. Herres.

"This also is the first time that a deal of this size has tapped the capital markets to facilitate the placement of reinsurance, an event that I believe is essential for the long-term strength of the nation's property and casualty insurers," he said.
Cat Bond Investors, a joint venture formed by PXRE Corp, said it was one of the investors in the bond offering, which was managed by Merrill Lynch, Goldman Sachs and Lehman Brothers.

"Our objective in selecting investments for the venture is to assume risk only when we are adequately compensated for that risk," Steven Goldstein, vice president of underwriting and trading for PXRE said in a recent statement.
"We believe our first investment is very attractive in that regard," he said. He said Cat Bond investors was currently examining other investment opportunities.

USAA's Herres said USAA has never had a loss of the magnitude of $1 billion, but said that size natural disaster is possible with large populations residing in coastal areas and other areas vulnerable to hurricanes.
The creative use of the domestic and international capital markets to facilitate reinsurance coverage is particularly suited to help manage USAA's financial exposure to large hurricanes, USAA said.

The reinsurance will apply to catastrophic property losses in the District of Columbia and 20 states: Alabama, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, Vermont and Virginia.
USAA long has purchased traditional reinsurance to cushion the association and its members from catastrophic losses.
The Residential Reinsurance layer will add to USAA's strong financial position within the property and casualty industry.
"We have transferred a considerable amount of risk, which benefits all of our policyholders," said Wilson C. Cooney, president of USAA Property and Casualty Insurance Group.
"This reinsurance also enhances USAA's ability to continue to serve members who live in hurricane-prone areas," he said.
"We expect that this form of reinsurance, when widely used by the industry, will help alleviate many of the property insurance availability problems associated with catastrophic risk," he said.
